Broken at Night, Reprinted in 2 Hours

published 2026-08-21 · in the recent-cohort window the advice is computed over · analysed 2026-09-01

1 · Retention breakdown

curve100 samples, stored one per percent runtime9:05 gone by 0:3048.3% at halfway31% still watching methodhazard = (present before − present after) ÷ present before at each moment; baseline = mean hazard of the previous 5 moments, floored; flagged when the excess viewers lost beyond baseline ranks high; a rise is a rewind only when no comparable drop precedes it and the lift survives the next sample

Red marks are flagged drops, green are earned rewinds. Hover a mark for its note.

2 · Each flagged moment: from curve to note

drop0:11
1 · what the curve showedA quarter of the opening audience walks during a five-second window explaining the grandfather's death (*2.8x the surrounding stop rate, 254 viewers, 81.0% to 65.6%*). 2 · evidence at that second“my grandfather Rudy passed away” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The cold open is a personal eulogy rather than the broken-bed premise the title promised: "my grandfather Rudy passed away." 4 · how (the next move)Cut 0:00-0:35 and open on the snapped leg at 3:57, then fold the grandfather context into the 4:35 bridge. 5 · rationaleThe 30-second mark holds 55.0% against a 66.6% channel median, beating only 16 of 148 — the eulogy opener is what puts this video in the bottom tenth.
drop4:16
1 · what the curve showedA 33-second window loses 137 viewers as the broken-leg show-and-tell pivots into a second grandfather monologue (*5.1x the surrounding stop rate, 32.8% to 24.5%*). 2 · evidence at that second“about a month ago, I lost my grandfather” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The build pauses mid-reveal to restate the loss: "about a month ago, I lost my grandfather." 4 · how (the next move)Cut 4:32-4:49 and go straight from the infill reveal into the top-down photo step at 6:11. 5 · rationaleThe spike sits at the exact seam where the physical diagnosis stops and personal framing restarts — removing the restatement keeps the reveal's momentum.
drop5:27
1 · what the curve showedThe steepest spike of the video lands as the BetterHelp read begins, quitting 108 viewers in 16 seconds (*11.4x the surrounding stop rate, 7.0x the channel norm*). 2 · evidence at that second“the sponsor of today's video, BetterHelp” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The sponsor arrives after the emotional beat has resolved: "that brings me to the sponsor of today's video, BetterHelp." 4 · how (the next move)Move the read to 4:15, right before the snapped-leg reveal, so it runs while the diagnosis is still teased rather than after the personal beat closes. 5 · rationaleSponsors hold best at the height of anticipation; here the read follows a released emotional beat, and stopRate at 7.0x the channel norm shows viewers treat it as their exit cue. cautionVerify BetterHelp's placement contract permits a mid-diagnosis slot; if locked to this position, A/B a 10-second cold tease of the reprint before the read instead.
peak6:05
1 · what the curve showedAudience climbs 19.8% and holds for 30 samples as the sponsor read ends and the CAD rebuild begins (*79 viewers regained, holding 18.8%*). 2 · evidence at that second“let's get back to the video” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers scrub back to the return-to-content cue: "Now, let's get back to the video." 4 · how (the next move)Front-load the CAD-and-print sequence to around 1:30 so the payoff viewers rewind to reach arrives before the 2:00 mark where only 33.6% remain. 5 · rationaleA replay peak on the reprint step proves this is the content the audience came for; it currently sits after two-thirds of them have left.
peak6:11
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises 13.0% and holds for 28 samples as the reprint workflow is introduced (*62 viewers regained, holding 21.3%*). 2 · evidence at that second“we're 3D printing a new part” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers rewind to the method statement: "we're 3D printing a new part." 4 · how (the next move)Merge this beat with the 6:16 photo step into a single opening sequence, and cut the redundant "what I actually did with this part" preamble. 5 · rationaleThree replay peaks cluster in eleven seconds around the reprint method — that density identifies the actual premise, and it belongs at the top of the video.
peak6:16
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises 11.6% and holds for 23 samples on the top-down photo-to-CAD step (*63 viewers regained, holding 23.7%*). 2 · evidence at that second“I took a picture top down” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers rewind to the concrete method: "I took a picture top down." 4 · how (the next move)Show the phone photo and the Shaper 3D redraw as the video's first act, before any narration about the bed. 5 · rationaleThe rewind proves the photograph-to-model trick is the transferable idea; leading with it delivers on the title's "Reprinted in 2 Hours" promise immediately.

drop0:00
1 · what the curve showedThe opening ten seconds bleed harder than almost any other video on the channel (*13.69% stop rate, 1.6x the channel norm, 324 viewers lost*). 2 · evidence at that second“put down their beloved dog” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The video opens on backstory about a dead pet before the build is teased: "had to put down their beloved dog, Titan." 4 · how (the next move)Cut 0:00-0:25 and open on the finished printed Titan from 10:51, then cut back to the sad setup. 5 · rationaleOnly 15 of 148 sibling videos hold worse at 0:15 — the promise of the thumbnail is buried behind a eulogy.
peak10:38
1 · what the curve showedAudience climbs into the print reveal and holds for four samples (*+5.2% of viewers present, 20 regained, audience at 24.9%*). 2 · evidence at that second“see how it actually came out” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers scrub back for the finished print reveal: "see how it actually came out." 4 · how (the next move)Front-load a two-second glimpse of this shot inside the first 15 seconds as the cold open. 5 · rationaleThis is the moment the audience treats as the payoff — using it as bait would rescue the 0:00 collapse.
peak10:47

drop10:57

peak12:32

drop12:42
1 · what the curve showedThe single sharpest drop of the video hits right after the final reveal (*9.54% stop rate, 9.2x the channel norm, 92 viewers lost in 38 seconds*). 2 · evidence at that second“pretty spitting images of” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The payoff has just been delivered and the audio shifts into a song: "pretty spitting images" then "[singing] long." 4 · how (the next move)Cut 12:37-13:20 and hard-cut from the side-by-side comparison into a tease for a second Titan with color. 5 · rationaleViewers feel released the moment the comparison lands; the song signals the video is over and they leave.

drop0:00
1 · what the curve showedThe opening sheds viewers at the channel's usual rate, actually a hair gentler than most uploads here (*7.89% vs 8.36% typical, 0.9x norm*). 2 · evidence at that second“got a new car” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Standard channel intro pattern — the premise is laid out plainly: "got a new car, and there's a couple things that I'd like to make improvements on." 4 · how (the next move)Hold the current cold open; do not recut an intro that already beats the channel median by 1.3pp. 5 · rationaleRewriting a first frame that outperforms 89 of 148 sibling videos risks trading a known win for an unknown.
peak6:21
1 · what the curve showedViewers scrub back as the first print is pulled early to check fit (*+2.1% audience, 46 viewers regained, held 20 samples*). 2 · evidence at that second“stop it right now” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The decision to abort the print is the hook: "still have 19 minutes left on it, but I think we're just going to stop it right now." 4 · how (the next move)Front-load a 6-second tease of this abort-and-test moment inside the first 30 seconds of the video. 5 · rationaleThe strongest sustained replay sits on a decision point, not the finished part — proving the process beats the product for this audience.
peak6:34
1 · what the curve showedAudience climbs again as the first physical fit-test happens on camera (*+2.0% audience, 45 viewers regained, held 17 samples*). 2 · evidence at that second“seems to fit” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The verdict is called out loud: "it is a little small in all directions... the actual curvature and the radius of the part seems to fit." 4 · how (the next move)Cut the 15 seconds of print-settings talk at 6:05-6:14 so the fit-test lands sooner after the design segment. 5 · rationaleTwo consecutive replay peaks on the same test beat prove viewers want the result faster; trimming setup shortens the wait without touching the payoff.
peak7:36

So, it's wider at the top, a little bit more narrow at the bottom." 4 · how (the next move)Show the three-to-four failed iterations on camera rather than jump-cutting past them at 7:20. 5 · rationaleViewers rewind to the moment a hidden constraint gets named — expanding that beat gives them more of what they already sought out.

I can go back at any point and change the entire layout." 4 · how (the next move)Hold the reveal walkthrough as-is; the loss here sits inside the channel's normal range for a payoff beat. 5 · rationaleMarked typical for channel at 1.1x norm — surgery here would chase noise while the real bleed sits at 10:05.
drop10:05
1 · what the curve showedSponsor read triggers the worst non-outro exit on the video, three times the channel's usual loss at this position (*3.2x spike, 3.0x channel norm, 203 viewers lost*). 2 · evidence at that second“use the code Mountain Maker 10” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The Shapr3D pitch lands after the reveal is over: "if you are interested in downloading Shapr3D... use the code Mountain Maker 10." 4 · how (the next move)Test moving the read to 6:17 while the first print is still running and the fit is unresolved. 5 · rationaleAds hold at the height of anticipation; running it after the payoff releases viewers who already got what they came for. cautionConfirm sponsor contract permits repositioning; if the placement is locked, tighten the read from 27s to under 15s instead.

drop0:00

drop4:17

drop0:00
1 · what the curve showedThe first 17 seconds shed nearly 40 points of audience, twice the rate the channel usually loses here (*10.9x the surrounding stop rate, 714 viewers, 98.9% down to 60.9%*). 2 · evidence at that secondno transcript line available; the note uses check-this-timestamp language 3 · why (the check or the quote)Check 0:00-0:17 for a cold-open or channel-branding beat that delays any cherry-nightstand payoff the thumbnail promised. 4 · how (the next move)Cut whatever runs before the first cherry-wood or nightstand shot and open on that shot with one line naming the build. 5 · rationaleThe channel's own median holds 79.4% at 0:15; this video sits at 87.4% then collapses to 49.3% by 0:30, so the loss lands inside the intro, not the hook frame.
peak5:58
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises 3.2% for a single sample around the two-fifths mark, regaining 14 viewers (*19.8% audience here, position 41%*). 2 · evidence at that secondno transcript line available; the note uses check-this-timestamp language 3 · why (the check or the quote)Check 5:58 for a brief technique moment — the rise is small and lasts one sample, so it reads as a quick scrub-back rather than a sustained reveal. 4 · how (the next move)Leave 5:58 in place and do not restructure around it; note the moment as a candidate for a Shorts clip instead. 5 · rationaleA one-sample rise is too shallow to justify editing, but it is strong enough to test as standalone short-form content off the main video.
drop7:42
1 · what the curve showedA 70-second stretch mid-build loses 35 viewers, but at a stop rate indistinguishable from the channel's norm here (*3.6x the surrounding rate, 0.86% vs 0.90% typical, 1.0x channel norm*). 2 · evidence at that secondno transcript line available; the note uses check-this-timestamp language 3 · why (the check or the quote)Check 7:42-8:52 for the kind of setup or measurement beat this channel routinely loses viewers on — the spike is local, not unusual. 4 · how (the next move)Leave the cut alone and instead trim any repeated measuring or clamp-adjusting shots inside the 70 seconds to under 20 seconds combined. 5 · rationaleStop rate matches the channel median exactly, so surgery here would not recover viewers the channel keeps elsewhere either.
peak8:26
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises 6.2% and holds three samples in the middle of the build, regaining 26 viewers (*19.8% audience here, position 58%*). 2 · evidence at that secondno transcript line available; the note uses check-this-timestamp language 3 · why (the check or the quote)Check 8:26 for a measurement being read out or a hidden-bracket detail — mid-build replays this sustained usually sit on a step viewers want to copy. 4 · how (the next move)Add an on-screen callout at 8:26 naming the exact dimension or hardware shown, and reference it from a pinned comment. 5 · rationaleSustained mid-build replays indicate a step people rewind to catch; making the number legible first time reduces the rewind and rewards the interest.
drop10:54
1 · what the curve showedA 52-second segment three-quarters through loses 28 viewers at roughly 1.6x the channel's usual rate for this position (*4.2x the surrounding stop rate, 1.43% vs 0.90% typical*). 2 · evidence at that secondno transcript line available; the note uses check-this-timestamp language 3 · why (the check or the quote)Check 10:54-11:46 for a finishing or sanding pass that repeats work already shown, since the drop runs above the channel norm rather than at it. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 10:54-11:46 to a single 15-second time-lapse of the finishing step and rejoin on the first assembled-nightstand shot. 5 · rationaleThe channel loses fewer viewers at this position on other builds, so the excess loss is specific to what this stretch shows, not the slot itself. cautionVerify the segment does not contain a load-bearing technique step; if it does, keep the step and cut only the repeated passes.
peak13:48
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises 9.0% and holds four samples into the final minute, regaining 31 viewers at the video's very end (*16.7% audience here, position 95%*). 2 · evidence at that secondno transcript line available; the note uses check-this-timestamp language 3 · why (the check or the quote)Check 13:48 for the finished-nightstand reveal or an on-wall install shot — the position and the sustained hold match a payoff viewers scrub back to. 4 · how (the next move)Cut a 6-second version of this reveal and paste it at 0:05 as the hook's proof-of-payoff, keeping the full reveal at 13:48. 5 · rationaleThe opening loses 60.6% in the first 5% with no visible payoff; showing the finished piece up front closes the interest gap the current intro leaves open. cautionVerify the reveal is not the video's only climactic frame; if it is, use a tighter or partial angle up front so 13:48 still lands.
